question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India states about the executive power of the Union?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 53**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 53** of the Constitution of India states that the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President.
 
• The President can exercise these powers either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.
 
• This article is a part of the larger framework that outlines the powers and duties of the executive branch of the government.
 
• It ensures that the executive authority is centralized under the President, thereby providing a unified command structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **President of India** is the head of state and the supreme commander of the armed forces.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college comprising the elected members of both houses of Parliament and the legislative assemblies of states and union territories.
 
• The executive power extends to the matters with respect to which Parliament has the power to make laws and to the exercise of such rights, authority, and jurisdiction as are exercisable by the Government of India by virtue of any treaty or agreement.
 
• The President also has the power to appoint the Prime Minister, who acts as the head of government, and other ministers based on the Prime Minister's advice.
 
• The Constitution of India provides a detailed framework for the distribution of powers between the executive, legislative, and judiciary branches to ensure a balanced governance structure.
